observations.finalText:
Saved **two pool-only options** and qualified contributions to candidate `01a15988-d5b4-7000-bd94-5d5f2ff0e349`. **All 60 selected cards remain unchanged.**

| Added option | Useful contribution | Qualification |
|---|---|---|
| **Focused Reader** | Draw-two access without sacrificing a creature; two eligible copies in Allowed 2. | Does not provide Feast Reader’s death-enabling function. |
| **Patient Supplier** | Repeatable `{2}` token production feeds the sacrifice/death engine; one eligible copy in Allowed 2. | Supplies bodies, not sacrifice access. Requires mana, a separate outlet and a payoff. |

### Engine comparison
- **Feast Reader:** conditional access requiring an existing creature. Two cards drawn is not automatically two net cards: counting the casting card and a sacrificed nontoken card, the draw transaction is card-neutral before retained-body or death benefits. Token fodder improves that exchange.
- **Feast Outlet:** repeatable sacrifice access, but consumes supply for life gain—not cards or opponent damage.
- **Feast Reward:** converts other controlled creatures’ deaths into opponent life loss; creates neither bodies nor deaths itself.
- **Focused Reader:** draw transaction is +1 without a sacrifice cost, but cannot replace the lost death-enabling function by itself.

These are synthetic accounting comparisons: bare draw text on incomplete Creature records does not establish real-MTG playability.

### Rejected misleading fits
- **Misleading Seed:** looking at and bottoming the top card draws nothing; its tags do not justify an access contribution.
- **Patient Supplier’s sacrifice tag:** does not make it an outlet.

### Remaining limits
The selected configuration still lacks repeatable creature production; pool alternatives supply **zero selected coverage**. Retrieval also found only one eligible copy each of Outlet and Reward against four selected—not a joint Availability determination.

All six discovered tag searches and the independent draw-two search were exhausted. This covers the supplied finite search populations, **not a whole-Collection census**. No completed-deck, legality or assemblability claim was made.

observations.finalText:
Saved **two pool-only options with qualified contributions**. The selected 60 and confirmed Brief/policy remain unchanged.

### Useful additions
- **Focused Reader:** Draws two without Feast Reader’s additional creature-sacrifice cost. Spending one hand card and drawing two yields **+1 hand card**; Feast Reader also consumes a board creature, offsetting that gain in material unless death benefits compensate. Focused Reader preserves bodies but loses the sacrifice event. These synthetic Creature cards’ bare draw text leaves retained-body/resolution accounting unspecified.
- **Patient Supplier:** Costs `{1}`, then `{2}` per 1/1 token, with no stated tap or turn limit. Supplies expendable bodies without spending further hand cards. Tokens feed Feast Reader or Feast Outlet and trigger Feast Reward when they die. This is renewable **board material**, not draw—and Supplier is **not an outlet**, despite its tag.

Both were discovered under the confirmed two-binder policy; no deck borrowing was used.

### Misleading fits and dependencies
- **Misleading Seed:** Looking at the top card and putting it on the bottom provides neither draw nor net card advantage. Its strong access/engine tags do not justify inclusion here.
- **Feast Outlet:** Sacrifices another creature for life, not cards; needs supply and a separate payoff.
- **Feast Reward:** Converts other controlled creatures’ deaths into opponent life loss, but supplies neither bodies nor sacrifice access.

### Remaining gaps
The unchanged fixture contains four copies each of Reader, Outlet and Reward plus 48 Meadows. Renewable supply remains **absent from selection**; pool options repair no active coverage. The broad “Engine support: 60” count is not meaningful functional coverage.

All six discovered synthetic-tag searches and the independent draw-two search exhausted their scoped results. No additional death payoff emerged. This was not a whole-Collection census, playable-deck assessment, or joint Availability check.
